## Solution

We want the last two digits of $f(17)+f(18)+f(19)+f(20)$ where $f(x)=x^{x^{x^x}}$, i.e. each value modulo $100$. Since $100=4\cdot 25$ with $\gcd(4,25)=1$, we use CRT, computing each $f(x)\bmod 4$ and $\bmod 25$.

**Key tool:** For $a^E \bmod 25$, since $\varphi(25)=20$, reduce $E\bmod 20$ (valid when $\gcd(a,25)=1$, which holds for $x\in\{17,18,19\}$).

---

### $f(17)\bmod 100$

- $\bmod 4$: $17\equiv 1$, so $17^{\text{anything}}\equiv 1\pmod 4$.
- $\bmod 25$: need $17^{(17^{17})}\bmod 25$, reduce exponent $17^{17}\bmod 20$.
  - $17\equiv -3\pmod{20}$, $(-3)^4\equiv 1$, so $(-3)^{17}=(-3)^{16}\cdot(-3)\equiv -3\equiv 17\pmod{20}$.
  - Now $17^{17}\bmod 25$: $17^2\equiv 14,\;17^4\equiv 21,\;17^8\equiv 16,\;17^{16}\equiv 6,\;17^{17}\equiv 6\cdot17=102\equiv 2\pmod{25}$.
- CRT: $\equiv 1\pmod 4,\;\equiv 2\pmod{25}$. Candidates $\equiv 2\pmod{25}$: $2,27,52,77$; only $77\equiv 1\pmod 4$.

$$f(17)\equiv 77\pmod{100}.$$

### $f(18)\bmod 100$

- $\bmod 4$: $18\equiv 2$, and $2^k\equiv 0\pmod 4$ for $k\ge 2$; the exponent $18^{18}\ge 2$, so $\equiv 0\pmod 4$.
- $\bmod 25$: reduce $18^{18}\bmod 20$. $18\equiv -2$, $(-2)^{18}=2^{18}=262144\equiv 4\pmod{20}$.
  - $18^4\bmod 25$: $18\equiv -7$, $(-7)^2=49\equiv -1$, so $(-7)^4\equiv 1\pmod{25}$. Thus $18^4\equiv 1$, and $18^{18^{18}}\equiv 18^4\equiv 1\pmod{25}$.
- CRT: $\equiv 0\pmod 4,\;\equiv 1\pmod{25}$. Candidates $\equiv 1\pmod{25}$: $1,26,51,76$; only $76\equiv 0\pmod 4$.

$$f(18)\equiv 76\pmod{100}.$$

### $f(19)\bmod 100$

- $\bmod 4$: $19\equiv -1$, exponent $19^{19}$ is odd, so $(-1)^{\text{odd}}\equiv -1\equiv 3\pmod 4$.
- $\bmod 25$: reduce $19^{19}\bmod 20$. $19\equiv -1\pmod{20}$, $(-1)^{19}\equiv 19\pmod{20}$.
  - $19^{19}\bmod 25$: $19\equiv -6$. The order of $-6$ mod $25$ is $10$ (since $(-6)^5\equiv -1$, $(-6)^{10}\equiv 1$). So $(-6)^{19}=(-6)^{10}\cdot(-6)^9\equiv (-6)^9\equiv (-6)^{-1}\pmod{25}$. The inverse of $-6\equiv 19$ is $4$ (since $19\cdot4=76\equiv 1$). So $\equiv 4\pmod{25}$.
- CRT: $\equiv 3\pmod 4,\;\equiv 4\pmod{25}$. Candidates $\equiv 4\pmod{25}$: $4,29,54,79$; only $79\equiv 3\pmod 4$.

$$f(19)\equiv 79\pmod{100}.$$

### $f(20)\bmod 100$

$20^2=400\equiv 0\pmod{100}$, and the exponent $20^{20}\ge 2$, so $20^{(20^{20})}\equiv 0\pmod{100}$.

$$f(20)\equiv 0\pmod{100}.$$

---

### Sum

$$77+76+79+0 = 232 \equiv 32\pmod{100}.$$

The last two digits of $f(17)+f(18)+f(19)+f(20)$ are $\boxed{32}$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
